evidence.clarity: H1 'Too lumpy today?' is swimmer vernacular, not a statement of the product; the lede ('reads the tide, wind, swell and water temperature at your beach and shows the windows when they line up for a swim') does the explaining. At 1440 and 390 a stranger gets it after the lede, and the CTA 'Join the public beta' plus 'iPhone. 40 beaches in the UK and Ireland so far.' makes the next step clear.
evidence.fit: Tone is the strongest of the pair for 'the sea at 6 am, not a weather app': light 300-weight sans on night water, and the bands get lighter section by section (#14212a to #d9e1e2) so the page literally goes from pre-dawn to grey morning. The 'Conditions, not permission' band and 'It won't nudge you to go in' handle the no-safety constraint. The 'replaces three sites and a group chat' line becomes its own section.
evidence.distinctiveness: Structure comes from the product: full-bleed tide line as the hero's horizon, background lightening down the page, a lock-screen notification (05:42, 'Your window now closes at 08:00') for the early warning, group-chat bubbles. Nothing like a template kit. The hero itself is very sparse (big headline, empty right half), which is a point of view rather than a stock layout.
evidence.proof: The tide chart starts in the first viewport and is operable: dragged the range and the chart at 1440/768/390, status cycled 'Window opens at 06:20' / 'In the window until 08:00 (1 h 20 min)' / 'Window closed early at 08:00. Last night it ran to 09:10' / 'No window for the rest of the morning'. Numbers are derived from one model and agree with the beach rows and notification. But at 1440 only the top of the chart is visible above the fold and its example caption sits below the readout.
evidence.craft: Deliberate type pairing (light sans display, Charter-style serif body) and generous rhythm. Defects: at 1440 the hero's right half (~700px) is empty above the chart; the chart labels only fade in after ~1.6s, so the first impression is an unlabelled curve; time-axis labels at 55% opacity are faint (axe flags one contrast node at 390 and 1440); the range input is 28px tall; the lock-screen card has no visible caption.
evidence.mobile: 390: recomposed sensibly. Headline, lede, CTA and the full-bleed chart with '06:10 now' and '06:20 to 08:00 swim window' are in the first screen; 'lost to the wind' label and minor hours hidden to avoid clutter; vals go 2-up; no overflow. Tapping the chart at 70% moved the cursor to 08:40 with status updating just below. Weak points: range target 28px, header 'Join the beta' 40px tall, and the example caption is ~350px below the first screen.
evidence.honesty: Beach rows say 'Example beaches and times.' and the readout caption says 'A made-up November morning at an example beach... Not a forecast.' But the hero chart shows a '06:10 now' pill and a 'swim window' band with no label in view at 1440 or 390; the caption only appears after scrolling past the readout. The lock-screen notification (dated 'Tuesday 17 November') has no visible example label at all (only an aria-label). The no-lifeguard message is handled well and the CTA goes to the brief's URL.
evidence.interaction: One control plus direct manipulation: range 'Drag through the morning' (ArrowRight x10 moved to 07:00 and updated status, cursor pill and four values) and pointer drag/tap on the chart both work at all three widths, aria-live on status, no console errors. Four distinct states handled. No other controls, no reset needed; the notification drop-in plays once on scroll. Thin rather than broken.
evidence.copy: Specific and British: 'Four tabs and a group chat, at half five', 'Sea temperature: Which gloves?', 'The number everyone asks for when you get out', 'wading back over the stones', 'Conditions, not permission', 'Swimming tomorrow morning?'. Every line carries information; no filler. Only the H1 is more hook than statement.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: headline, lede, CTA and the top band of the tide chart with '06:10 now', '06:20 to 08:00 swim window' and '08:00 to 09:10 lost to the wind' (after the 1.6s fade). 390: same stack with the chart and window label in view. The promise is specific but the in-view artifact is unlabelled as an example and the readout that explains it is below the fold; the right half at 1440 is dead space.

problems: Example labelling is late: the hero chart's '06:10 now' and swim-window band have no example label in the first screen at 1440 or 390, and the lock-screen notification has no visible label at all
1440 hero leaves the right half empty and shows only the top sliver of the artifact; the chart's labels only appear after a 1.6s animation
Small/faint details: 28px range target, 40px header link, 55%-opacity axis labels flagged by axe for contrast

evidence.clarity: H1 'Check the sea, not the group chat' plus lede 'an iPhone app for people who swim in the sea all year... turns the tide, wind, swell and water temperature at your beach into today's swim windows, and warns you when one closes early' says what, who and what changes. CTA 'Join the iPhone beta' with 'Opens the beta page.' Nothing later contradicts it.
evidence.fit: Every ask is visible: the 'three websites and a tide table' replacement is literally drawn as four source strips on one axis; the early-close warning gets its own before/after bar chart; 'It shows conditions. You make the call.' plus the 'What only you can read' ledger (flags, rips, how much cold you can take) is a deliberate, non-undermining resolution of the lifeguard constraint. Palette is pre-dawn with a sunrise gradient, but the four-strip section with wind arrows and swell bars reads like a surf-forecast dashboard, which brushes against 'not like a weather app'.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero artifact is a tide-curve portrait of a whole day with a dawn/dusk sky gradient keyed to sunrise 07:24 and sunset 18:06, windows as bands of first light, hatched 'Closes early: was 08:30'. A beach-orientation plan (offshore/onshore) and a cove cross-section with a swimmer and tow float are product-specific drawings. The surrounding frame (nav links, split headline/lede hero, CTA band) is more conventional than A's.
evidence.proof: The core job is operable in the first screen at 1440: clicked chips 07:00 ('Inside the morning window, 30 min left' + orange 'Closes early today at 07:30...'), 08:00 ('Outside the windows. The morning window closed early at 07:30. Next opens at 16:00.'), 17:00 ('Inside the evening window, 2 h 30 min left. It closes at 19:30.'); slider to 05:00, 15:00, 20:00 all give correct states. Chart, strips, before/after bars and readout share one sample day (05:30-07:30, was 08:30) and are labelled as a sample.
evidence.craft: Lora display + Inter text on a defined step scale, consistent 6px radii and rules, readout card has clear hierarchy (2.25rem time, bordered verdict, orange early note). Defects: dense hero chart with label collisions at 1440 ('Morning window 05:30-07:30' runs into the hatched early-close area, 'Closes early' and 'sunrise 07:24' chips crowd); at 390 with 08:00 selected the arrival line runs through the 'HW 06:24' label; many 13px chart labels; the cove illustration is flatter than the rest. One run at 1440 logged 'rect attribute width: A negative value' console errors that I could not reproduce.
evidence.mobile: 390: genuinely recomposed. The chart is redrawn at phone size with shortened labels ('05:30-07:30', 'was 08:30', hours every 4 h), example caption sits directly above it, chips are 44px, slider 44px, strips redraw with short row titles, cove tags thin out. Menu button opens a panel, Escape closes it, tapping 'Not a lifeguard' scrolls and closes it. Weak point: the verdict readout sits ~230px below the chips, so after tapping 08:00 near the bottom of the screen the text answer is below the fold (the chart above does move).
evidence.honesty: 'Sample day at a sample south-facing beach, written for this page. Not a forecast.' sits directly above the chart at every width; readout ends 'Conditions, not a verdict. You decide whether to swim.'; cove is captioned 'Illustration'; CTA notes say 'Opens the beta page' / 'Opens the beta page at tidewise.example.' before the click. Verdict copy says 'Inside the morning window', never safe. No invented numbers outside the labelled sample.
evidence.interaction: Chips, slider (ArrowLeft x5 from 17:00 to 16:35, chips correctly unselect), reset ('Reset to 06:00' restored 06:00), mobile menu with Escape and outside-click close, skip link. Every state has distinct text, light condition ('Dark until sunrise at 07:24', 'After sunset (18:06)') and early-close note toggles correctly. Feedback is split between the chart (moves at the tap) and the readout, which at 768/390 is below the controls. Transient console errors in one run.
evidence.copy: Specific and plain: 'Check the sea, not the group chat', 'Three websites and a tide table, on one line', 'from the tide table / from a surf forecast', 'What only you can read: How much cold you can take today, and who is swimming with you'. Slightly more explanatory and repetitive than A ('Sample day at a sample...beach, written for this page'; 'Opens the beta page' twice; the lede restated in the reads section).
evidence.first_screen: 1440: headline, what/who lede, CTA, the labelled sample-day chart with both windows and the early close, chips, slider and the readout ('Inside the morning window, 1 h 30 min left' + 'Closes early today at 07:30') all in one viewport. 390: headline, lede, CTA, sample label and the full chart are in view; chips start at the fold. The action label matches what happens.

problems: On 768 and 390 the verdict readout sits below the chips and slider, so the text answer to a tap can be off-screen
Hero chart is dense with small 13px labels that collide (morning window label into the hatch at 1440; arrival line through 'HW 06:24' at 390)
The four-strip forecast section and nav-plus-split-hero frame lean toward a weather-dashboard/template feel, against the brief's 'not like a weather app'

reason: B puts a labelled, fully operable sample day with the early-close warning in the first screen at both widths and states what the CTA does, so the promise is specific and believable before any scroll. A has the better mood and the better copy, and fits 'the sea at 6 am' more closely, but its artifact is only partly in view and unlabelled in the first screen, and its notification mock has no example label. If A moved its example caption into the hero and used the empty right half, I could prefer it for its tone.
